findings.summary: editRejectedDraftHandler does not patch metadata.authoringActivityIds with the new activity IDs after creating the edited draft. saveTeacherDraftHandler does this patch (line 476-483) but editRejectedDraftHandler omits it. After an edit, deleteLessonTree's orphan-cleanup path uses the stale (pre-edit) activity ID list, so non-primary activities from multi-activity sections become orphans on subsequent edits. The section-based cleanup path still handles primary activities, so lifecycle, publish gating, and student visibility are unaffected.

toTeacherFacingStatus default case uses 'return persistedStatus as TeacherFacingStatus' which would pass through an unrecognized status as-is rather than throwing. Safe in practice because the function is only called with known DB statuses (draft/review/approved/archived/published), but a defensive throw would be more robust.

notes: State machine verified: all allowed transitions (draft→review, review→approved, review→archived, approved→draft, archived→draft, approved→published) succeed; all illegal transitions (draft→published, review→published, archived→published, published→edit, non-draft→submit) are rejected. Idempotency verified: same key re-saves without duplicating rows. Sanitization verified: unsafe markup stripped before persistence. Hash integration verified: real computeComponentContentHash used, placement-derived componentKind (explore→activity, worked_example→example, guided_practice→practice) correct. Publish gating verified: stale approvals detected, missing approvals block publish. Authorization verified: teacher-scoped, ownership enforced, cross-teacher rejected. Student visibility verified: requires published + assigned class + active enrollment + same organization. Architecture verified: no parallel schema registry, no parallel hash/approval primitive, Convex wrappers thin, reuses existing tables. No A3 (digit-only count), A4 (vacuous pass), or A5 (false-claim text) violations. Plan.md claims match reality: targeted gate exits 0, aggregate failures documented as pre-existing.
